title: Kantianism
body:
**Kantianism** judges the action itself, leaving its consequences out of the assessment
entirely, and tests it against two formulations of the categorical imperative.

**Universalisability.** Act only on a rule you could will everyone to follow. A rule that
contradicts itself when universalised is prohibited: if everybody lied when it was convenient,
the practice of believing statements would collapse and lying would stop working, so the rule
undermines its own possibility.

**Humanity as an end.** Treat people as ends in themselves and never merely as means. Using
somebody purely as an instrument for an outcome is prohibited however good the outcome is.

Applied to technology, the second formulation does most of the work:

```
a system that judges an individual by a group statistic
    uses them as a means to efficiency
a dark pattern that manipulates a user into a purchase
    treats them as a mechanism to be triggered
a terms-of-service document written to be unread
    obtains consent while defeating its purpose
```

Its strength is that it produces firm answers where [[Utilitarianism]] produces arithmetic, and
it protects a minority from a favourable total. Its weakness is rigidity: two universal rules
can conflict in a specific case, and the framework offers no way to weigh them against each
other.
